words.hint: There's a silent C hiding in the middle: mus-C-le, like a secret muscle you can't see.
words.sentence: After the long swim, Maya could feel every muscle in her arms aching.

words.hint: A shirt has one Collar and two Sleeves: one C and two Ss.
words.sentence: It is necessary to wear a helmet when you ride your bike on the road.

words.hint: Start with a horse's neigh, then add bour: neigh + bour.
words.sentence: Our neighbour kindly looked after our cat while we were on holiday.

words.hint: U and I are a nuisance together: n-U-I-sance.
words.sentence: The wasp buzzing around our picnic was a real nuisance.

words.hint: Two cats can occupy a sofa: double C, but only one P.
words.sentence: Grandad brought some puzzle books to occupy us on the long train journey.

words.hint: Keep the house together and hold on: house + hold + d, with no letters lost.
words.sentence: Everyone in our household has a job to do on Saturday mornings.

words.hint: A relative is someone you can rely on, and there's an A in the middle: rel-A-tive.
words.sentence: We visited a relative in Scotland during the summer holidays.

words.hint: A farmer works on a farm: just farm + er.
words.sentence: The farmer drove his tractor slowly down the muddy lane.

words.hint: Utensil ends just like pencil: -sil, not -sel or -sle.
words.sentence: A wooden spoon is the most useful utensil in our kitchen drawer.

words.hint: Two Rs roll around inside the barrel, and it ends in -el.
words.sentence: The pirates rolled a heavy barrel of apples onto the ship.
